text:
This looks like September 2015, shortly after the August 2015 volatility spike.

- Unemployment is 5.3%, which fits mid-2015 (it was 5.1% in August and 5.3% in June or July).
- Fed funds is at 0.14%, with no hike yet. The first hike came in December 2015.
- The VIX is 26 and the 1-month US equity return is -6.1%, which points to August 2015, when the VIX spiked and the S&P fell about 6%.
- The trade-weighted dollar is up 16% year over year, and emerging-market equities are down sharply, both consistent with 2015.
- Headline CPI is at 0.21% year over year, which matches the summer of 2015.

Unemployment of 5.3% matches July 2015 (5.3%) better than August (5.1%). Data published at the end of August would show the July unemployment rate, so the snapshot is most likely August 2015. The VIX of 26.05 is plausible for the August 31 close (about 28), and the -6.1% monthly equity return matches August.

I settle on August 2015.
